payload.title: Autonomy-closure evidence pins and verifies only the frozen findings.jsonl blob: the event logs that `project --stdin --ref` folds are neither chain-verified nor named in the evidence refs, so registry_chain_valid_at_evidence_target claims more than it checks
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/autonomy_closure.py:312-333 (_registry_snapshot reads that blob and cites {evidence}:findings.jsonl@<blob> as the evidence ref)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/autonomy_closure.py:366 (`verify --stdin` runs the chain test on the blob's bytes alone)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/autonomy_closure.py:380 (`project --stdin --ref` then reads the event logs at the ref, with no chain test on them)
payload.rule_violated: MF-DESIGN section 4.3: an evidence pin of the registry is the git tree id of docs/reviews/_registry at the evidence commit, and the chain predicate verifies everything the closure verdict reads
payload.notes: The blob is frozen, so the cited ref {evidence}:findings.jsonl@<blob> is the same string for every event state. A corrupted or rewritten event log at the evidence commit leaves registry_chain_valid_at_evidence_target true and the ref unchanged, and the closure verdict is computed from logs whose hash chains nobody checked on this path. The verdict is correct for logs that hold; the claim of a verified registry is wider than the check. Read from the code, not probed. Close condition: The predicate verifies the whole store at the evidence target (the genesis blob and every event log's chain, through the registry CLI that owns the test) and the evidence ref names the tree id of docs/reviews/_registry. A test where a log with a broken chain at the evidence commit makes the predicate false.
